frozen_decisions_applied: Plan #1, verbatim: 'Remove kProvisioningApPassword = "12345678" and every shared/default production secret.' -- the constant no longer exists anywhere in this repository; the AP passphrase is generated fresh every boot from hardware RNG and never persisted, satisfying 'removed' rather than 'replaced with a different fixed value'.

Plan #4, verbatim: 'Provisioning AP SSID includes a non-secret gateway suffix; its passphrase is exactly 16 cryptographically random Base32 characters and uses WPA2/WPA3 settings supported by target.' -- implemented exactly: SSID suffix reuses plan #9's own last-6-hex-of-GatewayId convention; passphrase is exactly 16 Base32 characters from 10 real random bytes; hal_wifi_start_ap() now uses the real WIFI_AUTH_WPA2_WPA3_PSK mixed mode.

Plan #6, verbatim: 'Generate session and CSRF secrets from hardware RNG.' -- implemented as the reusable generate_random_secret_hex() primitive; the actual session/CSRF subsystem that will call it is a later, separate S6 sub-slice ('HTTPS and sessions').

User's explicit, asked-for decision on passphrase delivery (no plan-text resolution existed for this display-less-device question): log the freshly-generated passphrase via ESP_LOGI at AP start, matching plan #2's own sanctioned interim posture for its analogous PoP-material case, with a named tracked follow-up for a real production channel.

hal_random_implemented.detail: hal_random_fill_bytes() wraps the real esp_fill_random() (confirmed signature and exact documented true-randomness condition via a real grep inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5 before writing any code -- 'If Wi-Fi or Bluetooth are enabled, this function returns true random numbers', quoted directly rather than overclaiming an unconditional guarantee). Host fallback is an explicitly non-cryptographic PRNG used only so host tests can observe real variation; no production code path executes it.

base32_implemented.detail: Unpadded RFC 4648 Base32 encoder in components/common (matching GatewayId's own no-ESP-IDF-dependency component boundary). Verified against Python stdlib base64.b32encode() reference vectors computed fresh for this sub-slice, not hand-derived or recalled from memory, including the exact 10-byte input shape ('AAAQEAYEAUDAOCAJ') this project's real passphrase generator produces.

provisioning_secrets_implemented.detail: generate_provisioning_passphrase() (10 random bytes -> 16 Base32 chars, tied by static_assert to SecurityBounds::kProvisioningPassphraseBase32Chars from S6 slice 1), generate_random_secret_hex() (generic hex-secret primitive for plan #6, bounded at 64 bytes defensively), build_provisioning_ap_ssid() (prefix + last-6-hex-of-GatewayId, reusing plan #9's own naming convention).

hal_wifi_wpa2_wpa3_updated.detail: hal_wifi_start_ap() now sets WIFI_AUTH_WPA2_WPA3_PSK (confirmed real symbol via grep inside esp_wifi_types_generic.h) instead of WIFI_AUTH_WPA2_PSK -- mixed mode accepts both WPA2-only and WPA3-capable admin clients, satisfying plan #4's WPA2/WPA3 text with the broadest compatibility choice for a provisioning network.

app_main_wired.status: COMPLETE -- first real production behavior change since S5 began
app_main_wired.detail: main/app_main.cpp no longer has any hardcoded provisioning secret. Every boot that starts the provisioning AP generates a fresh SSID (via build_provisioning_ap_ssid) and passphrase (via generate_provisioning_passphrase), fails closed (halts with a logged error, does not fall back to any default) if either generation call fails, and logs the passphrase via ESP_LOGI with explicit 'development-only console delivery' wording pointing at this document.

real_bug_found_and_fixed.status: COMPLETE -- found only by the real ESP-IDF target build
real_bug_found_and_fixed.detail: The first version of the app_main.cpp change referenced SecurityBounds::kProvisioningPassphraseBase32Chars without the service:: namespace qualifier. main/app_main.cpp is not part of test/host/CMakeLists.txt at all (it is ESP-IDF-application-entry-only code), so the host build could never have caught this -- only a real idf.py build could, and did (a real compiler error: 'SecurityBounds has not been declared'). Fixed with the missing qualifier; confirmed via a second, clean full real build (10/10 steps after the fix, ccache-accelerated since only app_main.cpp and its dependents needed rebuilding).

tests_and_verification.detail: 4 tests in test_hal_random.cpp, 7 in test_common_base32.cpp (including the 2 Python-computed reference vectors), 11 in test_provisioning_secrets.cpp -- 22 new test assertions total. Full repository host suite: 95/95 passing (92 pre-existing + 3 new test executables). cppcheck: zero findings against all 4 changed/new C/C++ files (base32.cpp, hal_random.c, provisioning_secrets.cpp, hal_wifi.c). check_arch_invariants.sh: high=0/medium=0/low=0, unchanged. Two separate real idf.py builds inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5: the first failed with the real namespace-qualifier bug above; the second, after the fix, succeeded end-to-end, confirming the new production wiring actually compiles and links against the real ESP32-C6 target.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Only plan #1, #4 and #6 are implemented; #2 (ProvisioningSecretProvider port for manufacturing PoP material), #3 (commissioning-window enforcement) and #5 (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 admin password verifier) remain unimplemented, even though the user selected the whole '#1-6' cluster.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: The six items are not one coherent unit of work -- #1/#4/#6 share one underlying primitive (hardware-RNG-derived secrets) and together remove the literal hardcoded value the plan names by exact string; #2/#3/#5 are each substantial, distinct pieces (a new port abstraction, a state machine consuming Section 2.1's commissioning-window tunable, and a calibrated PBKDF2 implementation) that do not share that primitive and deserve their own sub-slices, matching this project's established per-item sub-slicing discipline throughout S5 and S6 slice 1.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: The provisioning AP itself is now secure (random passphrase, WPA2/WPA3), but there is still no commissioning-window expiry, no manufacturing PoP verification, and no admin password enrollment mechanism -- the AP alone does not yet constitute a complete, secure provisioning flow.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The provisioning passphrase is delivered to the installer via an ESP_LOGI console log line, not a real production out-of-band channel (printed label, QR code, or similar).
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: This device has no display, only UART, and no real manufacturing/labeling process exists yet in this sandbox; the user was asked directly and confirmed this interim mechanism, matching plan #2's own sanctioned precedent for its analogous PoP-material case.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: In a real manufacturing deployment, logging the passphrase to a serial console is not a viable production delivery mechanism (most end users have no UART access) -- a real channel must be designed before this project has real production users, tracked as a named follow-up likely to land alongside plan #2's own work.
